transitions.priorTeaching: Earlier chapters distinguish firm output, market quantity, periods and units. No prior labour-market formula is presumed.
transitions.newTeaching: 431 introduces persons, paid hours, fte, output per hour and full labour cost per unit before a numerical example. Derived labour demand is explained through orders and productivity; movement along a curve and a shift are separately illustrated.
transitions.boundary: A given output needs fewer hours at higher productivity; employment cannot be inferred without output and hours per person. The final wage-and-orders scenario is explicitly new and has unknown magnitudes. Higher productivity alone guarantees neither jobs nor profit.

transitions.boundary: Population counts and sector-model quantities concern different groups. Participation percentages are not unemployment percentages; their difference is percentage points. Each fictional sector explicitly supplies hours per person and wage domain.

transitions.priorTeaching: 432 supplies workforce definitions, the separate population/sector contexts and solving a free labour-market equilibrium.
transitions.newTeaching: 433 explicitly introduces the workforce denominator for unemployment, vacancy and matching distinctions, causes of unemployment, and a demand shock under first flexible then fixed wages.
transitions.boundary: Vacancies are unfilled places, not employed people; unemployment minus vacancies is not unemployment. A flexible-model loss of jobs is not automatically the same number unemployed. A fixed wage is a separate stated assumption, not a claim that all regional unemployment has that cause.

transitions.priorTeaching: 433 explicitly compares a flexible wage with a fixed wage after a demand shock. Book3§3.1.5 teaches a price floor without automatic government purchases.
transitions.newTeaching: 434 introduces the minimum wage as a lower bound, tests whether it binds against the free equilibrium, then distinguishes actual employment, extra labour supply and total excess supply. It teaches payroll as wage times paid hours times employed persons before independent work.
transitions.boundary: A nonbinding floor leaves the free equilibrium feasible. A binding floor is not a demand shift or government hiring promise. Individual retained-worker pay can rise while group payroll falls. The own example uses24 hours, target25; conditions are explicitly reset.
